reviewer: Codex merchant owner, actual images inspected

views.name: hull_rig
findings: The two-mast schooner carries separate long gaff sails, a fore square topsail and triangular forward canvas; the raked spars, stays and ratlines remain distinct against the grey background.
The low ochre planked hull retains a long row of gun stations, shallow raised ends and a green transom with external rudder; open deck lanes and framed accesses remain readable beneath the rig.
views.scope: Whole actual GLB with all visible hull, rig and sails.

views.name: deck_closeup
findings: The timber-coamed hatch opens into a complete sloping stair with separate pale treads, side strings, upright posts and rope handrails; the lower sole and yellow inner planking are visible through the opening.

Fine longitudinal grain and staggered seams cover the pale deck. The horizontal wooden windlass and paired bitts appear beside the hatch, while scratched dark gun barrels and wooden carriages give the edge a material contrast.
views.scope: Actual deck and fitting close-up at a fixed 4.5 metre physical field; rig hidden for visibility.

views.name: hold_interior
findings: The intact hold shows curved framing, separate hanging knees and overhead beams against the ochre inner strakes; lengthwise grain is visible on the pale sole and the large frame members.

One full-size crew berth with mattress and pillow, a strapped locker with a ring-handled lantern, and the complete access stair share the enclosed room. The clear sole beside the stair and berth remains readable at adult eye height.

Compared with the matched original Brig hold, the visible frame sequence, ceiling structure and separate berth/locker joinery make the internal construction substantially more explicit; the review fill reveals the farther frame bays.
views.scope: Camera inside the actual enclosed GLB room; auxiliary camera fill reveals timber and furniture.

views.name: hold_cutaway
findings: The cutaway exposes the long planked sole, curved frame sequence, timber access flights, side berths, casks and locker fittings, making the connected floor layout readable from above.

The small dark galley assembly is visible beside the forward stair and framing. Original upper guns, pins and rig fittings remain visible while their enclosing hull/deck layers are hidden only for this view.
The broad cutaway is brightly lit and small furniture details are less distinct at this framing; the separate intact view provides the closer material and enclosure evidence.
views.scope: Read-only cutaway: named outer hull, upper deck timbers and bulkheads temporarily hidden; delivered GLB unchanged.

views.name: cabin_interior
findings: The open framed doorway gives a direct view of the separate companion stair beyond; the planked cabin sole leaves a readable route between the furniture, below explicit ceiling beams and curved side frames.

The chart desk, full berth with mattress and pillow, bench/lantern and strapped chest are visibly separate wooden assemblies. The close-stool in the foreground has a raised hinged lid and a genuinely open seat over the dark pot.

At the matched 20 mm lens and 1.23 m eye height, the cabin has substantially more legible grain, framing, furniture and actual access detail than the original Brig reference; the original enclosure remains intact in this view.
views.scope: Camera inside the actual enclosed GLB room; auxiliary camera fill reveals timber and furniture.

views.name: cabin_cutaway
findings: The cutaway exposes the berth, lantern on a separate bench, chest and close-stool through the retained curved framing; the pale planked sole continues across the after room.

The frame ends, horizontal inner strakes and deck structure remain explicit around the furniture. Retained upper guns and fittings appear above the room only because enclosing hull and roof layers are temporarily hidden for this view.
views.scope: Read-only cutaway: named outer hull, upper deck timbers and bulkheads temporarily hidden; delivered GLB unchanged.
